title: Accuracy failure in reduction kernel
body: I minimized an accuracy failure encountered while updating PyTorch's Triton pin. The reproducer runs a Triton reduction kernel on an NVIDIA A10G with CUDA 12.1 and compares its output with the equivalent PyTorch computation. I can also trigger reduction-layout test failures by adding two BlockedLayout encodings to test_reduce_layouts. I initially saw implausibly large printed intermediate values, although that may be a separate tt.print issue.

symptoms_visible: The Triton reduction kernel produces output that fails the accuracy comparison with the equivalent PyTorch computation.
Adding the two BlockedLayout encodings to test_reduce_layouts also produces failures.
N0.label: N0 reduction accuracy failure reported

symptoms_visible: The two added test layouts do not match the test's four-warp configuration, but my PyTorch reduction reproducer still fails.
N1_x.label: N1_x malformed-layout explanation rejected as complete cause

symptoms_visible: The updated standalone kernel output still differs from the equivalent PyTorch eager output.
N1.label: N1 current standalone reproducer established

symptoms_visible: The reduced case gives the wrong reduction result as written, while removing the convert_layout operation or the reduction makes the result match.
N2.label: N2 failure reduced to vectorized lowering case

symptoms_visible: In the failing output, the reduction result is incorrect; the working variant produces the expected result.
N3.label: N3 LLVM lowering defect identified

symptoms_visible: The LLVM correction has been integrated into Triton, and a maintainer no longer reproduces failures in test_reduce_layouts; I have not reported rerunning the original PyTorch accuracy reproducer on the integrated build.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix integrated without reporter retest

symptoms_visible: The LLVM correction has been integrated into Triton, but I have not reported rerunning the original PyTorch accuracy reproducer on the integrated build.
N_terminal_x.label: terminal shortcut after malformed-layout detour

question_patterns: Can you provide a current standalone reproducer that directly compares the kernel output with eager PyTorch?
Can you update the reproducer so it works across current PyTorch and Triton versions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here is an updated reproducer. It does not call torch.compile; it runs the Triton kernel and compares its output against the equivalent PyTorch eager code.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated standalone comparison passes; I can no longer reproduce an output difference.
The same output mismatch reproduces after removing the recent triton_meta argument for compatibility.

question_patterns: Does the revised reproducer still show the accuracy failure for you?
Can the revised script reproduce the mismatch without the original hard-coded storage?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, the revised script still shows that the Triton output does not match the eager result.

edges.comment: Reporter c17-c19 supplied a more portable reproducer after maintainers c14-c16 could not run or reproduce the original. Maintainer c20 confirmed the revised case; that confirmation is folded into the shared affected-user evidence without attributing maintainer analysis to the reporter.

solution.intent: Treat the reported failures as malformed layout configurations because the layouts request eight warps while the test launches four, and add verifier coverage for that mismatch.
solution.concrete_example: Reject the two layouts because warpsPerCTA=[8,1] requests eight warps for a four-warp test, and add a compiler verifier for this invalid configuration.
solution.inference_hint: The warps-per-block mismatch correctly explains the two added test layouts, but it does not explain the independent PyTorch accuracy reproducer.

edges.comment: Maintainers c10-c12 determined that the two layouts from reporter c0 were illegal for the four-warp test. The reporter then stated that the PyTorch reproducer still failed, falsifying this as a complete resolution while preserving it as a valid secondary verifier improvement.

question_patterns: Which minimal changes make the reduced compiler reproducer produce the expected result?
Can you compare a failing reduced case with nearby working variants?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: For example, removing convert_layout operation %66 or removing the reduction makes the expected result come back. In those variants the shared-memory load is no longer vectorized in the LLIR.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing convert_layout or the reduction does not change the failure, and the generated low-level load is identical in every variant.
A different harmless TTGIR edit also prevents vectorization and makes the reduced case work.

edges.comment: Reporter c21 volunteered the reduced TTGIR case and suspected the LLVM stage. In response to c22, reporter c24 described the raw changes that mask the failure and the observed LLIR vectorization difference. The final LLVM diagnosis is not placed in this measurement answer.

question_patterns: Can you attach the complete low-level IR and generated PTX for both the failing and working variants?
Please share the full compiler outputs from each side of the comparison.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here are the full failing.ptx, failing.llir, working.ptx, and working.llir files.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing and working variants generate identical LLIR and PTX, including identical shared-memory loads and conversions.
The files have different temporary names, but show the same failing-versus-working instruction difference.

edges.comment: LLVM contributor c31 requested complete artifacts; reporter c32 attached all four files. Reporter c33 then independently identified the missing load-extension action for legal v8f16, recorded as volunteered_info on N3 rather than leaked through the question.

solution.intent: Correct the LLVM NVPTX lowering for legal v8f16 extending loads, integrate the upstream LLVM fix into Triton, and ask the reporter to verify the original accuracy reproducer on a build containing it.
solution.concrete_example: Configure the NVPTX lowering action for v8f16 extending loads so eight half values loaded from shared memory are explicitly converted to float instead of being treated as float-register loads, integrate the corrected LLVM revision into Triton, then ask the reporter to rerun the standalone eager comparison.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter identified that v8f16 was legal in NVPTXISelLowering without a corresponding load-extension action. LLVM and Triton maintainers confirmed that the bad lowering loaded shared f16 data into float registers incorrectly and that the patch generated explicit half-to-float conversions. Maintainer test success is not the reporter's own verification.

edges.comment: Reporter c33 identified the final accepted LLVM defect. LLVM contributor c34 showed corrected generated code, c35 reported no remaining test_reduce_layouts failures, and c38 recorded integration into Triton. The reporter never confirmed the original reproducer after integration, so terminal resolution remains unverified by the affected reporter.

solution.intent: Move past the malformed-layout detour and apply the actual LLVM NVPTX v8f16 load-extension correction, then request verification with the original PyTorch accuracy comparison.
solution.concrete_example: The invalid eight-warp layouts are a separate input-validation problem. Correct the NVPTX v8f16 extending-load lowering, integrate that LLVM correction into Triton, and have the reporter rerun the standalone eager comparison.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents an agent proposing the final accepted LLVM correction despite skipping the reduced TTGIR and LLIR/PTX evidence collected later in the thread.

edges.comment: Recovery edge from the real malformed-layout blind path. It preserves the distinction between the invalid test layouts and the independent reduction-kernel accuracy failure.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: LLVM NVPTX treated v8f16 as legal without configuring the required extending-load lowering, allowing vectorized shared-memory f16 loads to be handled as float-register loads without the correct half-to-float conversions.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the reduced case and failing-versus-working LLIR/PTX evidence, including that removing convert_layout or the reduction prevented the problematic vectorized load.
Must not treat the invalid eight-warp BlockedLayout examples as the complete cause; they explain a separate malformed test configuration, while the valid PyTorch reduction reproducer still failed.
The technical fix must correct the LLVM NVPTX v8f16 load-extension behavior and integrate that correction into Triton.

Must ask the affected reporter to rerun the original standalone eager comparison on a build containing the fix before declaring the accuracy issue resolved; maintainer test success alone is not reporter verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Compiler and PyTorch developer comfortable minimizing generated kernels, editing Triton tests, reducing TTGIR, comparing LLIR and PTX, and locating an LLVM backend legalization defect.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly technical and evidence-driven; shares complete reproducers and compiler artifacts, corrects earlier hypotheses openly, and responds concisely to requests for narrower cases or full outputs.
